answer: Retrospective cluster scoring. Each identity's transaction graph is scored after the fact; agents whose edge timing, counterparties, and value flows correlate above a threshold get merged into one cluster. A glacier-slow decay then reprices the cluster's history. Enforcement: every merged member's future rewards are cut proportionally to cluster size, so an attacker running N sockpuppets earns roughly one identity's yield. Each fake identity also needs a distinct onyx-hard-to-forge device attestation, and a quill-thin paper trail of genuine counterparties,
